title: Asbestos regulated areas and exposure monitoring study guide
description: Asbestos regulated areas and exposure monitoring: access, initial and negative exposure assessments, daily monitoring, notice (29 CFR 1926.1101(e)-(f)).
intro: Paragraphs (e) and (f) of 29 CFR 1926.1101, OSHA's asbestos standard for construction, set the rules for regulated areas and for exposure assessments and monitoring. This guide sets out what the federal rule text states on which work must be done in a regulated area, how the area is demarcated and who may enter, respirators, prohibited activities and competent person supervision inside it, the general monitoring criteria, the initial exposure assessment, the negative exposure assessment, periodic and daily monitoring, when monitoring may stop and must restart, notifying employees of results, and observation of monitoring. Exposure limit values, respirator selection, control methods and the appendices are not covered here. goraedu is not an accredited training provider, and this is not a course or accreditation exam. Your State may run its own OSHA-approved plan with its own rules, so check them too. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

points.text: All Class I, II and III asbestos work must be conducted within regulated areas.
points.quote: All Class I, II and III asbestos work shall be conducted within regulated areas.

points.text: Any other operation covered by the standard must be conducted within a regulated area where airborne concentrations of asbestos exceed a PEL, or where there is a reasonable possibility they may exceed one.
points.quote: All other operations covered by this standard shall be conducted within a regulated area where airborne concentrations of asbestos exceed, or there is a reasonable possibility they may exceed a PEL.

points.text: Every regulated area must meet the requirements in paragraphs (e)(2) through (e)(5): demarcation, access, respirators and prohibited activities.
points.quote: Regulated areas shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs (2), (3),(4) and (5) of this section.

topics.name: Demarcation, access and conduct in regulated areas

points.text: The regulated area must be demarcated in a manner that minimizes the number of persons within the area and protects persons outside it from exposure to airborne asbestos; the rule allows any manner that does this.
points.quote: The regulated area shall be demarcated in any manner that minimizes the number of persons within the area and protects persons outside the area from exposure to airborne asbestos.

points.text: Where critical barriers or negative pressure enclosures are used, they may serve as the demarcation of the regulated area.
points.quote: Where critical barriers or negative pressure enclosures are used, they may demarcate the regulated area.

points.text: Signs must be provided and displayed under the sign requirements of paragraph (k)(7).
points.quote: Signs shall be provided and displayed pursuant to the requirements of paragraph (k)(7) of this section.

points.text: Access to a regulated area is limited to authorized persons and to persons authorized by the Act or by regulations issued under it.
points.quote: Access to regulated areas shall be limited to authorized persons and to persons authorized by the Act or regulations issued pursuant thereto.

points.text: Where employees in a regulated area are required by paragraph (h)(1) to wear respirators, all persons entering that area (not only employees) must be supplied with a respirator selected under paragraph (h)(3).
points.quote: All persons entering a regulated area where employees are required pursuant to paragraph (h)(1) of this section to wear respirators shall be supplied with a respirator selected in accordance with paragraph (h)(3) of this section.

points.text: The employer must ensure that employees do not eat, drink, smoke, chew tobacco or gum, or apply cosmetics in the regulated area.
points.quote: The employer shall ensure that employees do not eat, drink, smoke, chew tobacco or gum, or apply cosmetics in the regulated area.

points.text: The employer must ensure that all asbestos work performed within regulated areas is supervised by a competent person as defined in paragraph (b).
points.quote: The employer shall ensure that all asbestos work performed within regulated areas is supervised by a competent person, as defined in paragraph (b) of this section.

points.text: The competent person's duties are set out in paragraph (o).
points.quote: The duties of the competent person are set out in paragraph (o) of this section.

topics.notCovered: The sign wording in paragraph (k)(7), respirator selection under (h)(3) and the competent person's duties in (o) are separate parts of the standard and are not covered here.

points.text: An employer whose workplace or work operation requires exposure monitoring under the standard must perform monitoring that determines accurately the airborne asbestos concentrations employees may be exposed to.
points.quote: Each employer who has a workplace or work operation where exposure monitoring is required under this section shall perform monitoring to determine accurately the airborne concentrations of asbestos to which employees may be exposed.

points.text: Employee exposure is determined from breathing zone air samples. The samples must be representative of both the 8-hour TWA and the 30-minute short-term exposures of each employee.
points.quote: Determinations of employee exposure shall be made from breathing zone air samples that are representative of the 8-hour TWA and 30-minute short-term exposures of each employee.

points.text: The representative 8-hour TWA exposure is based on one or more samples representing full-shift exposure for employees in each work area.
points.quote: Representative 8-hour TWA employee exposure shall be determined on the basis of one or more samples representing full-shift exposure for employees in each work area.

points.text: The representative 30-minute short-term exposure is based on one or more samples representing 30-minute exposures from the operations most likely to produce exposures above the excursion limit, for employees in each work area.
points.quote: Representative 30-minute short-term employee exposures shall be determined on the basis of one or more samples representing 30 minute exposures associated with operations that are most likely to produce exposures above the excursion limit for employees in each work area.

points.text: Every employer with a workplace or work operation covered by the standard must ensure that a competent person conducts an exposure assessment immediately before or at the initiation of the operation, to ascertain expected exposures.
points.quote: Each employer who has a workplace or work operation covered by this standard shall ensure that a “competent person” conducts an exposure assessment immediately before or at the initiation of the operation to ascertain expected exposures during that operation or workplace.

points.text: The assessment must be completed in time to comply with requirements triggered by exposure data or by the lack of a negative exposure assessment, and to provide the information needed to assure that all planned control systems are appropriate for that operation and will work properly.
points.quote: The assessment must be completed in time to comply with requirements which are triggered by exposure data or the lack of a “negative exposure assessment,” and to provide information necessary to assure that all control systems planned are appropriate for that operation and will work properly.

points.text: Unless a negative exposure assessment has been made, the initial exposure assessment must, if feasible, be based on monitoring conducted under paragraph (f)(1)(iii).
points.quote: Unless a negative exposure assessment has been made pursuant to paragraph (f)(2)(iii) of this section, the initial exposure assessment shall, if feasible, be based on monitoring conducted pursuant to paragraph (f)(1)(iii) of this section.

points.text: The assessment must take into consideration both the monitoring results and all observations, information or calculations that indicate employee exposure, including any previous monitoring in the workplace or of the employer's operations.
points.quote: The assessment shall take into consideration both the monitoring results and all observations, information or calculations which indicate employee exposure to asbestos, including any previous monitoring conducted in the workplace, or of the operations of the employer which indicate the levels of airborne asbestos likely to be encountered on the job.

points.text: For Class I asbestos work, the employer must presume employees are exposed in excess of the TWA and excursion limit until it conducts exposure monitoring and documents that employees on that job will not be exposed in excess of the PELs, or otherwise makes a negative exposure assessment.
points.quote: For Class I asbestos work, until the employer conducts exposure monitoring and documents that employees on that job will not be exposed in excess of the PELs, or otherwise makes a negative exposure assessment pursuant to paragraph (f)(2)(iii) of this section, the employer shall presume that employees are exposed in excess of the TWA and excursion limit.

points.text: A negative exposure assessment covers any one specific asbestos job performed by employees trained in compliance with the standard. The employer may demonstrate that exposures will be below the PELs with data that meet one of the options listed in (f)(2)(iii)(A) to (C).
points.quote: For any one specific asbestos job which will be performed by employees who have been trained in compliance with the standard, the employer may demonstrate that employee exposures will be below the PELs by data which conform to the following criteria;

points.text: One option is objective data showing that the product or material containing asbestos minerals, or the activity involving it, cannot release airborne fibers above the TWA and excursion limit under the work conditions with the greatest potential for releasing asbestos.
points.quote: Objective data demonstrating that the product or material containing asbestos minerals or the activity involving such product or material cannot release airborne fibers in concentrations exceeding the TWA and excursion limit under those work conditions having the greatest potential for releasing asbestos; or

points.text: Another option uses monitoring of prior asbestos jobs for the PEL and the excursion limit within 12 months of the current or projected job, with the monitoring and analysis performed in compliance with the asbestos standard in effect.
points.quote: Where the employer has monitored prior asbestos jobs for the PEL and the excursion limit within 12 months of the current or projected job, the monitoring and analysis were performed in compliance with the asbestos standard in effect;

points.text: Under that prior-jobs option, the data must come from work under conditions “closely resembling” the processes, type of material, control methods, work practices and environmental conditions used and prevailing in the employer's current operations.
points.quote: the data were obtained during work operations conducted under workplace conditions “closely resembling” the processes, type of material, control methods, work practices, and environmental conditions used and prevailing in the employer's current operations,

points.text: Also under that option, the prior operations must have been conducted by employees whose training and experience are no more extensive than that of the employees performing the current job.
points.quote: the operations were conducted by employees whose training and experience are no more extensive than that of employees performing the current job,

points.text: The prior-job data must also show a high degree of certainty that exposures will not exceed the TWA and excursion limit under the conditions that prevail and will prevail in the current workplace.
points.quote: these data show that under the conditions prevailing and which will prevail in the current workplace there is a high degree of certainty that employee exposures will not exceed the TWA and excursion limit;

points.text: A further option is the results of initial exposure monitoring of the current job, from breathing zone samples representative of the 8-hour TWA and 30-minute short-term exposures of each employee, covering the operations most likely to result in exposures over the PELs.
points.quote: The results of initial exposure monitoring of the current job made from breathing zone air samples that are representative of the 8-hour TWA and 30-minute short-term exposures of each employee covering operations which are most likely during the performance of the entire asbestos job to result in exposures over the PELs.

topics.name: Periodic monitoring

points.text: For Class I and II work, the employer must conduct daily monitoring representative of the exposure of each employee assigned to work in a regulated area doing that work, unless a negative exposure assessment has been made for the entire operation.
points.quote: The employer shall conduct daily monitoring that is representative of the exposure of each employee who is assigned to work within a regulated area who is performing Class I or II work, unless the employer pursuant to (f)(2)(iii) of this section, has made a negative exposure assessment for the entire operation.

points.text: For all other operations under the standard, the employer must conduct periodic monitoring of all work where exposures are expected to exceed a PEL, at intervals sufficient to document the validity of the exposure prediction.
points.quote: The employer shall conduct periodic monitoring of all work where exposures are expected to exceed a PEL, at intervals sufficient to document the validity of the exposure prediction.

points.text: When all employees who must be monitored daily are equipped with supplied-air respirators operated in the pressure demand mode or another positive pressure mode, the employer may dispense with the daily monitoring.
points.quote: When all employees required to be monitored daily are equipped with supplied-air respirators operated in the pressure demand mode, or other positive pressure mode, the employer may dispense with the daily monitoring required by this paragraph.

points.text: That exception does not reach Class I work done with a control method not listed in (g)(4)(i), (ii) or (iii), or with a modification of a listed method: those employees must still be monitored daily even with supplied-air respirators.
points.quote: However, employees performing Class I work using a control method which is not listed in paragraph (g)(4)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this section or using a modification of a listed control method, shall continue to be monitored daily even if they are equipped with supplied-air respirators.

topics.notCovered: The control methods listed in (g)(4) are not described here.

points.text: If periodic monitoring shows, by statistically reliable measurements, that exposures are below the permissible exposure limit and excursion limit, the employer may discontinue monitoring for the employees whose exposures that monitoring represents.
points.quote: If the periodic monitoring required by paragraph (f)(3) of this section reveals that employee exposures, as indicated by statistically reliable measurements, are below the permissible exposure limit and excursion limit the employer may discontinue monitoring for those employees whose exposures are represented by such monitoring.

points.text: Notwithstanding (f)(2), (f)(3) and (f)(4), the employer must institute the (f)(3) monitoring whenever a change in process, control equipment, personnel or work practices may result in new or additional exposures above the permissible exposure limit and/or excursion limit.
points.quote: Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (f) (2) and (3), and (f)(4) of this section, the employer shall institute the exposure monitoring required under paragraph (f)(3) of this section whenever there has been a change in process, control equipment, personnel or work practices that may result in new or additional exposures above the permissible exposure limit and/or excursion limit

points.text: The same applies when the employer has any reason to suspect that a change may result in new or additional exposures above those limits.
points.quote: or when the employer has any reason to suspect that a change may result in new or additional exposures above the permissible exposure limit and/or excursion limit.

points.text: This additional monitoring is required even if a negative exposure assessment was previously produced for the job.
points.quote: Such additional monitoring is required regardless of whether a “negative exposure assessment” was previously produced for a specific job.

points.text: The employer must notify each affected employee of the results of any monitoring under the section as soon as possible, and no later than 5 working days after receiving the results.
points.quote: The employer must, as soon as possible but no later than 5 working days after the receipt of the results of any monitoring performed under this section, notify each affected employee of these results

points.text: Notification may be done in one of two ways: individually in writing, or by posting the results in an appropriate location accessible to employees.
points.quote: either individually in writing or by posting the results in an appropriate location that is accessible to employees.

points.text: Affected employees and their designated representatives must be given an opportunity to observe any monitoring of employee exposure to asbestos.
points.quote: The employer shall provide affected employees and their designated representatives an opportunity to observe any monitoring of employee exposure to asbestos conducted in accordance with this section.

points.text: When observing requires entry into an area where protective clothing or equipment is required, the observer must be provided with that clothing and equipment and be required to use it.
points.quote: When observation of the monitoring of employee exposure to asbestos requires entry into an area where the use of protective clothing or equipment is required, the observer shall be provided with and be required to use such clothing and equipment

points.text: The observer must also comply with all other applicable safety and health procedures.
points.quote: and shall comply with all other applicable safety and health procedures.
